text:
Earthquake Faults
San Jose lies within 15 miles of all three major fault zones of the San Francisco Bay Region. The San Andreas Fault Zone is 11 miles to the southwest, while the Hayward and Calaveras Fault zones lie 5 and 7.5 miles, respectively, to the northeast. The east foothills of San Jose are traversed by several active faults. The Quimby Fault is approximately one mile east of the eastern edge of the Mayfair CNRA and the Evergreen Fault is approximately 1.75 miles southeasterly of the proposed site of the Meadowfair Park. The potentially active Silver Creek Fault bisects San Jose from the Evergreen foothills to the Bay. The earthquake activity criteria adopted by the California Division of Mines and Geology used to designate active and potentially active faults exclude the Silver Creek Fault from the Special Studies Zone required by the Alquist-Priolo Geologic Hazard Zones of 1972. Nevertheless, the Silver Creek Fault is of particular concern because it has been projected beneath the San Jose urban area by several investigators.
Various geologic studies have suggested different surface locations of the Silver Creek fault traces. Because of the difficulty in delineating a fault trace in alluvium, the approximate boundaries of a zone which probably contains much narrower traces are mapped in the Geotechnical Investigation. The following excerpt from that study describes the current assessment of the Silver Creek Fault:
"The activity of the northern portion of the Silver Creek Fault (that portion which passed beneath the urban area) has not been resolved. There is no compelling geologic evidence of past rupture at the surface of the Santa Clara alluvium. However, alluvium is highly erodible and if surface rupture occurred in the area before earthquake records were maintained (about 150 years), it could have easily been obliterated. However, in the hill area south of Evergreen, where the Silver Creek Fault traverses less erodible bedrock areas, the location of the fault trace is quite evident and is accompanied by topographic features, such as sag ponds, which strongly suggests that the last stage of activity has been quite recent. Therefore, on the basis of limited surface observations, it is our opinion that the Silver Creek Fault should be considered active south of the Evergreen area and at least potentially active in the northern area where it projects beneath urban areas. This urban area contains numerous schools, hospitals, and other major or critical structures. If this fault undergoes rapid surface rupture, extensive damage and loss of life could occur." *
The boundaries of the Silver Creek Fault zone encompass all of the developed area of Alviso and include approximately half of the Northside CNRA. The Mayfair CNRA is approximately one-half mile easterly of the zone and the Meadowfair Park site is almost adjacent to the fault zone boundary.
* Technical Report: Geotechnical Lavestigation, City of San Jose's Sphere of Influence, Cooper-Clark and Associates, 1974.
